verdict.justification: A provides the stronger executive negotiation guide because it turns the capacity advantage into a quantified last-time-buy strategy rather than making continuity depend on a much longer extension from an unwilling supplier. Its proposal for “5,200 by ~W10” at ramp capacity, with completion around W15 at base capacity, is more commercially attractive than B’s request for supply through April–June 2027. A also gives clearer concession exchanges, issue-by-issue negotiating boundaries, accountable transition milestones, and escalation triggers. B offers useful protections, including a standstill request and explicit air-freight contingency, but its tooling-release window is insufficiently reconciled with its local qualification schedule. B additionally introduces a provisional “+10–12%” premium authority without a cost basis, whereas A appropriately requires Finance and the CPO to establish the ceiling. A still needs substantial compression for the requested 2–3 pages, and its early plastics mould-out and transfer-inclusive development assumption require validation, but its central strategy is more actionable and better suited to securing LPI’s cooperation.
